moneyTrail.label: H.R.815 — Israel Security Supplemental
moneyTrail.detail: Signed into law. Passed House 366-58, Senate 79-18. Includes $4B for Iron Dome replenishment, $3.5B for weapons procurement, $1.2B for Iron Beam, $1B for artillery munitions.

moneyTrail.label: 10-Year MOU (2016) — Annual Baseline
moneyTrail.detail: Automatic annual aid: $3.3B in Foreign Military Financing + $500M for missile defense. Israel is the only recipient allowed to spend FMF on its own defense industry.

moneyTrail.label: Trump releases 1,800 MK-84 bombs
moneyTrail.detail: President Trump released a Biden-era hold on 1,800 MK-84 2,000-pound bombs immediately upon taking office. Each MK-84 costs ~$3,100 bare; with JDAM kits, ~$25,000 each.

moneyTrail.label: Foreign Military Financing → Weapons Procurement
moneyTrail.detail: FMF grants used to purchase: F-35 stealth fighters, Apache attack helicopters, MK-84 bombs, JDAM guidance kits, 155mm artillery shells, Hellfire missiles, and small-diameter bombs.

moneyTrail.label: Iron Dome / David's Sling Replenishment
moneyTrail.detail: Tamir interceptors ($50K–$100K each) and David's Sling Stunner missiles ($1M+ each). Used to defend Israeli territory from rocket attacks while offensive operations continue in Gaza.

moneyTrail.label: Artillery & Critical Munitions Production
moneyTrail.detail: 155mm artillery shells, tank ammunition, and other ground-force munitions used in the Gaza ground invasion. 155mm shells have been documented striking residential areas.

moneyTrail.label: MK-84 Bombs → Documented Civilian Impact
moneyTrail.detail: MK-84 2,000-pound bombs identified in: al-Mawasi "safe zone" attack (90+ killed, July 2024), Jabalia refugee camp strikes (120+ killed, Oct 2023), and numerous residential building collapses. Lethal blast radius: 360 meters.

moneyTrail.label: JDAM-Guided Strikes → Residential Areas
moneyTrail.detail: A $680M package of Joint Direct Attack Munitions (JDAM) kits and small-diameter bombs approved November 2024. JDAMs convert unguided "dumb bombs" into GPS-guided munitions — but in Gaza's density (6,500 people/km²), even "precision" strikes kill civilians.

moneyTrail.label: 155mm Artillery → Civilian Areas
moneyTrail.detail: 155mm artillery, designed for open-battlefield use, has been fired into one of the most densely populated areas on Earth. Each shell has a casualty radius of 50+ meters. Used extensively during the Jabalia and Nuseirat operations.

moneyTrail.label: CRS lifetime U.S. aid obligations (1946–2024)
moneyTrail.detail: Congressional Research Service RL33222 estimates $174.965B in current dollars through 2025 and roughly $298B in constant 2024 dollars through 2024 — the long-run public-record floor for U.S. financial enablement of Israeli military capacity.

moneyTrail.label: Pro-Israel lobby / PAC spend (2024 cycle)
moneyTrail.detail: OpenSecrets aggregates more than $180M in pro-Israel industry political spending for the 2024 cycle (PACs, outside spending, and related vehicles). This is campaign-finance enablement of the congressional aid floor — not a weapons transfer — and is tracked separately from FMF/MOU dollars.

moneyTrail.label: F-35 Joint Strike Fighter fleet (FMF-financed)
moneyTrail.detail: Israel is the first international operator of the F-35I Adir. Aircraft and sustainment are financed largely through U.S. Foreign Military Financing under the MOU architecture. F-35s provide the long-range strike backbone used in multi-theater operations; exact sortie attribution to specific Gaza strikes is not always public.

moneyTrail.label: U.S. War Reserve Stockpile Allies-Israel (WRSA-I)
moneyTrail.detail: The U.S. maintains a prepositioned munitions stockpile in Israel (WRSA-I) that can be drawn down in wartime under U.S. law and presidential authority. Drawdowns during the Gaza war accelerated munitions availability beyond annual FMF purchases alone. Tracked separately because stockpile release is a delivery mechanism, not a new appropriation.

moneyTrail.label: AGM-114 Hellfire missiles (FMF / wartime resupply)
moneyTrail.detail: U.S.-made Hellfire air-to-ground missiles are a core precision munition for Israeli attack helicopters and drones. DSCA notices and wartime resupply reporting document continued transfers under FMF and emergency drawdowns. Documented in strikes affecting civilian areas; specific strike-to-missile attribution is often incomplete in open sources.

moneyTrail.label: GBU-39 Small Diameter Bomb (SDB)
moneyTrail.detail: The GBU-39 SDB is a GPS-guided 250-pound-class bomb transferred under U.S. FMF and wartime packages. Marketed as reducing collateral damage relative to heavier munitions, it remains a high-explosive weapon used in dense urban targeting. Tracked as a distinct precision munition class from MK-84/JDAM heavy bombs.

moneyTrail.label: U.S. munitions industrial base surge funding
moneyTrail.detail: Congress funded expansion of U.S. artillery and precision-munitions production capacity partly to replenish stocks drawn down for Ukraine and Israel transfers. This is enablement of the supply chain itself — distinct from a single FMF line item — and appears in supplemental appropriations and DoD industrial-base budget materials.

moneyTrail.detail: AIPAC-affiliated Super PAC independent expenditures targeting federal races based on Israel-policy positions. OpenSecrets documents ~$37.9M in IEs and ~$87M raised in the 2023–2024 cycle — electoral enablement parallel to FMF appropriations.

moneyTrail.label: Iron Beam High-Energy Laser — Supplemental Line

moneyTrail.label: Post–Oct 7 Emergency Arms Transfer Surge
moneyTrail.amount: tens of thousands of munitions + multi-billion wartime packages
moneyTrail.detail: After October 7, 2023, the United States accelerated emergency munitions transfers (including 155mm, precision bombs, interceptors) via FMF, presidential drawdown authority, and WRSA-I stockpile releases — a delivery surge layered on top of the annual MOU, later consolidated partly through H.R.815 and related packages. moneyTrail.detail: J Street is the leading progressive pro-Israel PAC/advocacy network: supports a two-state framework and conditionality debates while remaining within pro-Israel security assistance politics. moneyTrail.detail: NORPAC is a long-running bipartisan pro-Israel PAC (New Jersey–rooted) that bundles and contributes multi-million cycle totals across party lines. moneyTrail.label: Republican Jewish Coalition — Conservative Pro-Israel
moneyTrail.detail: The Republican Jewish Coalition (RJC) is the primary Republican-aligned pro-Israel political network, directing multi-million cycle contributions predominantly to Republican candidates who lock in unconditional FMF and wartime orthodoxy. Chapter-14 FEC synthesis cites ~$5.6M scale — the GOP-side counterpart to Democratic DMFI/UDP and progressive J Street poles.

moneyTrail.label: U.S. Qualitative Military Edge (QME) Doctrine
moneyTrail.detail: U.S. law and executive practice commit to maintaining Israel's "qualitative military edge" over regional adversaries — a structural doctrine that shapes arms-transfer approvals, FMF levels, and third-country sales reviews. Distinct from a single appropriation: QME is the policy floor that makes wartime resupply and MOU architecture the default rather than exceptional.

moneyTrail.label: U.S. THAAD Battery Deployment to Israel
moneyTrail.detail: The United States deployed a Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) battery and U.S. service members to Israel to reinforce missile defense during the expanded Iran/Hezbollah threat environment. Distinct from FMF-financed Israeli systems: this is direct U.S. force posture enablement of Israeli air defense.

moneyTrail.label: Israel Emergency Supplemental (~$14.3B request track)
moneyTrail.detail: Post–October 7 White House/Congress emergency Israel security assistance request track (~$14.3B scale in public reporting) that fed into the larger supplemental architecture culminating in H.R.815 and related packages. Distinct from the annual MOU baseline — wartime emergency enablement layered on top of the $3.8B/year floor.

moneyTrail.label: FMF Cash-Flow Financing Privilege
moneyTrail.detail: Israel is among a small set of FMF recipients authorized to use multi-year cash-flow financing — signing contracts for U.S. weapons before annual appropriations fully arrive. This structural privilege accelerates weapons pipeline continuity beyond annual MOU cash and is documented in CRS RL33222 as a distinctive enablement feature of the U.S.–Israel aid relationship.

moneyTrail.label: U.S. UNSC Veto / Diplomatic Cover Pattern
moneyTrail.detail: The United States has cast dozens of Security Council vetoes shielding Israel from binding censure, plus selective abstentions (e.g., 2334, 2728). Post–October 7 vetoes of ceasefire drafts document continued diplomatic cover concurrent with FMF/weapons enablement. Distinct from cash aid — this is diplomatic-legal enablement of operational freedom.

moneyTrail.label: U.S.–Israel Joint Missile Defense Co-Production
moneyTrail.detail: U.S. and Israeli industry co-produce interceptor systems (Iron Dome Tamir, David's Sling, Arrow) with U.S. appropriations funding Israeli industrial capacity. Distinct from pure FMF purchases of U.S. inventory — this is co-production enablement of Israel's layered air defense industrial base, documented in CRS and DSCA materials.

timeline.title: The Balfour Declaration
timeline.description: British Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour writes to Lord Rothschild: "His Majesty's Government view with favour the establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people." Britain controlled neither the land nor the consent of its 700,000 Arab inhabitants.
timeline.source: The Avalon Project — The Balfour Declaration

timeline.title: King David Hotel Bombing — 91 Killed
timeline.description: Irgun bombs British Mandate HQ in the King David Hotel. 91 dead including British, Arab, and Jewish victims. Foundational Mandate-era atrocity with multi-source documentation.

timeline.title: UN Partition Plan (Resolution 181)
timeline.description: The UN General Assembly votes to partition Palestine into Jewish and Arab states, granting 56% of the land to the Jewish state despite Jews comprising 33% of the population and owning 7% of the land. Arab states reject the plan.

timeline.title: Deir Yassin Massacre
timeline.description: Irgun and Lehi forces kill roughly 100–200+ Palestinian villagers at Deir Yassin. The massacre accelerates mass flight and becomes a foundational event of the Nakba.

timeline.title: Lydda–Ramle Expulsions
timeline.description: Israeli forces expel tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians from Lydda and Ramle. Hundreds die on the forced march. Among the largest single expulsions of 1948.

timeline.title: The Nakba — 750,000 Palestinians Expelled
timeline.description: During the 1948 Arab-Israeli War, approximately 750,000 Palestinians are expelled or flee from their homes. Over 400 Palestinian villages are depopulated and destroyed. Israel declares independence on May 14.
timeline.source: UN Conciliation Commission for Palestine, Final Report

timeline.title: Qibya Raid Condemned by UN Security Council
timeline.description: Unit 101 kills 69 villagers in Qibya. UNSC Resolution 101 condemns the attack. Ariel Sharon commands the unit.

timeline.title: Kafr Qasim Massacre — Israeli Court Convictions
timeline.description: Border Police kill 49 Palestinian citizens of Israel for a curfew many had not been told about. Israeli courts convict perpetrators and articulate the "manifestly illegal order" doctrine.

timeline.title: Khan Yunis Mass Killings during Sinai Campaign
timeline.description: Israeli forces enter Khan Yunis during the 1956 war. Contemporary UN and later historical accounts document mass killings of Palestinian residents — one of the deadliest episodes of the brief 1956 Gaza occupation.

timeline.title: Al-Samu Raid Condemned by UN Security Council
timeline.description: Israeli raid demolishes houses in as-Samu and kills dozens. UNSC Resolution 228 condemns the large-scale military action — a major pre-1967 escalation.

timeline.title: Six-Day War — Occupation Begins
timeline.description: Israel captures the West Bank, Gaza Strip, Sinai Peninsula, and Golan Heights. Military occupation of Palestinian territories begins — now in its 58th year. UN Security Council Resolution 242 calls for Israeli withdrawal.

timeline.title: USS Liberty Attack — 34 Americans Killed
timeline.description: Israeli air and naval forces attack the USS Liberty, a clearly marked U.S. Navy intelligence ship, in international waters off the Sinai Peninsula. 34 American servicemen killed, 171 wounded. Israel calls it a case of mistaken identity; surviving crew members and multiple investigations dispute this.
timeline.source: U.S. State Department FRUS, Vol. XIX, Document 284

timeline.title: Munich Olympics Massacre — 11 Israeli Athletes Killed
timeline.description: Black September hostage-taking at the Munich Olympics ends with eleven Israeli athletes dead. Multi-source official and historical record.

timeline.title: Ma'alot School Massacre — Children Hostages Killed
timeline.description: DFLP school hostage crisis in Ma'alot kills 25 hostages, mostly children. Multi-source civilian-child targeting record.

timeline.title: Land Day — Six Palestinian Citizens Killed
timeline.description: Security forces kill six Palestinian citizens of Israel during protests against Galilee land expropriation. March 30 becomes an annual commemorative date.

timeline.title: Camp David Accords — U.S. Aid Escalates
timeline.description: Israel and Egypt sign the Camp David Accords, brokered by President Carter. As part of the deal, the U.S. commits to $3 billion/year in military and economic aid to Israel and $2 billion/year to Egypt — permanently reshaping U.S. foreign aid.

timeline.title: Coastal Road Massacre — 38 Israeli Civilians
timeline.description: Fatah bus hijacking/massacre on the Coastal Road kills 38 civilians including 13 children. Triggers Operation Litani.

timeline.title: Operation Litani — UNIFIL Created
timeline.description: Israel invades southern Lebanon. Large civilian displacement and casualties prompt UNSC Resolutions 425/426 establishing UNIFIL.

timeline.title: Operation Peace for Galilee — Lebanon Invasion
timeline.description: Israeli invasion of Lebanon produces mass civilian displacement and casualties documented by UN/HR orgs.

timeline.title: Sabra and Shatila Massacre
timeline.description: Israeli-allied Lebanese Phalangist militia massacres between 800 and 3,500 Palestinian and Lebanese Shia civilians in the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps. Israeli forces surround the camps and provide illumination. The Kahan Commission finds Defense Minister Ariel Sharon bears "personal responsibility."

timeline.title: Siege of West Beirut — Civilian Bombardment
timeline.description: Israeli siege and bombardment of West Beirut kills and displaces large numbers of civilians before PLO evacuation. Distinct from the later Sabra and Shatila camp massacre.

timeline.title: Beirut Marine Barracks Bombing — 241 U.S. Dead
timeline.description: Suicide truck bomb kills 241 U.S. Marines and 58 French paratroopers in Beirut.

timeline.title: Kahan Commission — Indirect Responsibility for Sabra/Shatila
timeline.description: Official Israeli commission finds indirect responsibility for Phalangist massacre; Sharon resigns as defense minister.

timeline.title: First Intifada Begins
timeline.description: Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation. Over six years, 1,551 Palestinians and 422 Israelis are killed. Defense Minister Yitzhak Rabin orders soldiers to "break their bones" — a policy documented by B'Tselem.
timeline.source: B'Tselem — Israeli Information Center for Human Rights

timeline.title: Oslo Accords
timeline.description: Israel and the PLO sign the Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government. Intended as a 5-year interim arrangement leading to a final status agreement. That agreement never materializes. Settlement population triples in the years following Oslo.

timeline.title: Cave of the Patriarchs Massacre
timeline.description: Settler Baruch Goldstein kills 29 Palestinian worshippers in Hebron. Israeli investigation and international record confirm the civilian massacre.

timeline.title: Qana UN Compound Shelling — 106 Civilians Killed
timeline.description: Israeli artillery hits a UNIFIL compound sheltering civilians in Qana, Lebanon. UN investigation challenges the accidental-error account.

timeline.title: Second Intifada — Multi-Thousand Civilian Death Toll
timeline.description: Roughly 3,000+ Palestinians and ~1,000 Israelis killed. Pattern record of suicide bombings against Israeli civilians and Israeli military operations causing mass Palestinian civilian casualties, tracked by B'Tselem and UN agencies.

timeline.title: Dolphinarium Discotheque Bombing — 21 Dead
timeline.description: Hamas bombing outside a Tel Aviv youth discotheque kills 21, mostly teenagers. Multi-source civilian-targeting record.

timeline.title: Sbarro Pizzeria Bombing — 15 Killed (7 Children)
timeline.description: Hamas suicide attack on Jerusalem restaurant during Second Intifada; multi-source death toll established.

timeline.title: Jenin Camp — Operation Defensive Shield Depth
timeline.description: UN/HRW multi-source documentation of camp battle deaths and destruction during Defensive Shield.

timeline.title: Jenin Camp Assault — UN Corrects Massacre Inflation
timeline.description: Heavy fighting and house demolitions in Jenin. UN finds ~52 Palestinian dead — serious civilian harm, not the hundreds initially claimed. Included to defeat both denial and exaggeration.

timeline.title: Park Hotel Passover Massacre — Netanya
timeline.description: Hamas suicide bombing at a Passover seder kills 30 civilians. Immediate prelude to Operation Defensive Shield.

timeline.title: ICJ Rules Separation Wall Illegal
timeline.description: The International Court of Justice rules 14-1 that Israel's construction of a wall in the occupied Palestinian territory is contrary to international law. Israel ignores the ruling. The wall is now 712 km long, 85% built inside the West Bank.
timeline.source: International Court of Justice, Advisory Opinion

timeline.title: Operation Days of Penitence — Northern Gaza
timeline.description: Major northern Gaza offensive. Monitors record ~100+ Palestinian dead including many civilians; widespread housing destruction in Jabalia/Beit Hanoun area.

timeline.title: Operation Rainbow — Rafah House Demolitions
timeline.description: Major Rafah offensive. HRW documents mass home demolitions and civilian deaths in southern Gaza.

timeline.title: Taba Hilton Bombing — Israeli Tourists Killed
timeline.description: Suicide car bomb at Taba Hilton kills dozens of mostly Israeli tourists; multi-source death toll.

timeline.title: Gaza Disengagement — Settlements Evacuated
timeline.description: Israel removes settlements and bases from Gaza while retaining control of airspace, waters, and most crossings — the prelude architecture to the post-2007 blockade.

timeline.title: Beit Hanoun Artillery Strike Kills 19
timeline.description: Israeli artillery hits a residential area in Beit Hanoun. 19 Palestinians killed, many of them women and children. UN and HRW demand investigation.

timeline.title: Dahiya Doctrine — Disproportionate Force Concept
timeline.description: IDF officers articulate disproportionate-force doctrine after Beirut Dahiya destruction; cited in later campaign analysis.

timeline.title: Operation Summer Rains — Gaza Offensive
timeline.description: Months-long Gaza offensive after Shalit capture. Monitors document hundreds of Palestinian deaths and major civilian-infrastructure damage including power generation.

timeline.title: Second Lebanon War — ~1,000+ Lebanese Dead
timeline.description: 34-day war. HRW/Amnesty document majority-civilian Lebanese deaths and cluster-munition contamination. Distinct from the single Qana building strike entry.

timeline.title: Gaza Blockade Begins
timeline.description: Following Hamas's takeover of Gaza, Israel imposes a land, air, and sea blockade. The UN and ICRC describe it as collective punishment of 2 million civilians. The blockade continues for 19 years.

timeline.title: Gaza Blockade Formalized
timeline.description: After Hamas takes control of Gaza, Israel and Egypt formalize a comprehensive blockade. UN agencies document multi-year civilian access and goods restrictions.

timeline.title: Cast Lead — Goldstone Fact-Finding Mission

timeline.title: Goldstone / HRW — White Phosphorus in Gaza Urban Areas

timeline.title: Mavi Marmara Flotilla Raid

timeline.title: Operation Pillar of Defense
timeline.description: Eight-day Gaza war. 160+ Palestinians killed per monitor tallies; six Israelis killed by rockets. U.S. aid and Iron Dome support continue under the standing MOU architecture.

timeline.title: Gaza Power Plant Struck — Protective Edge
timeline.description: Israeli strikes cripple Gaza's sole power plant, cascading into water, sewage, and hospital failures for the civilian population.

timeline.title: Operation Protective Edge — 2,251 Palestinians Killed

timeline.title: Palestine Accedes to Rome Statute — ICC Jurisdiction Opens

timeline.title: UNSC Resolution 2334 — Settlements Illegal

incidents.title: King David Hotel Bombing (Irgun)
incidents.location: King David Hotel, Jerusalem (British Mandate administrative HQ)
incidents.summary: The Irgun Zionist paramilitary organization bombed the southern wing of the King David Hotel, which housed British Mandate administrative and military headquarters. Ninety-one people were killed — British officials, Arab and Jewish hotel workers and visitors — in one of the deadliest attacks of the Mandate period.
incidents.evidence: British Mandate inquiries, contemporaneous press, and later archival historiography (including Irgun admissions of responsibility) establish Irgun authorship and the death toll. Included for chronological balance: civilian and administrative deaths by a Zionist paramilitary before statehood, with checkable primary-period documentation — not as collective blame of any people.

sources.label: British National Archives — Palestine Mandate records (catalog entry point)

incidents.title: Deir Yassin Massacre
incidents.summary: Irgun and Lehi paramilitary forces attacked the Palestinian village of Deir Yassin during the civil war phase preceding Israeli statehood. Estimates of those killed range roughly from about 100 to over 200, including women and children. The attack became a pivotal trauma in Palestinian collective memory and accelerated flight from other villages.
incidents.evidence: Contemporary Red Cross and British Mandate reporting, survivor testimony, and later archival work by Israeli and Palestinian historians document a deliberate assault on a civilian village. Exact death toll remains disputed among historians; the fact of a large-scale killing of non-combatants is not seriously contested in the scholarly record.

sources.label: UN Conciliation Commission — historical refugee documentation context
Jewish Virtual Library — contemporaneous source compilation (use critically)

multimedia.label: UNISPAL — 1948 refugee and war documentation index

incidents.title: Lydda and Ramle Expulsions
incidents.summary: During Operation Dani, Israeli forces captured Lydda and Ramle. Tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians were expelled on foot toward the West Bank in extreme heat. Hundreds died from exhaustion, dehydration, and related violence. These expulsions are among the largest single population removals of the 1948 war.
incidents.evidence: Israeli military orders, IDF archival material cited by historians (including Benny Morris), UN refugee registration, and survivor testimony document mass expulsion. Death estimates for the march vary; the forced removal of the majority civilian population is documented.

sources.label: UN Conciliation Commission for Palestine — Final Report context

incidents.title: Qibya Raid — Unit 101
incidents.summary: Israeli special forces Unit 101, commanded by Ariel Sharon, raided the West Bank village of Qibya. Sixty-nine Palestinian villagers were killed, more than half of them women and children. Homes were dynamited with occupants inside. The raid followed cross-border fedayeen attacks, but the scale of civilian killing drew international condemnation.
incidents.evidence: UN Security Council Resolution 101 (1953) condemned the action. U.S. and UK diplomatic protests are on record. Israeli official and later historical accounts acknowledge the raid and the civilian death toll.

sources.label: Britannica — Ariel Sharon biographical record of Qibya

incidents.title: Kafr Qasim Massacre
incidents.summary: Israeli Border Police shot and killed 49 Palestinian citizens of Israel — including women and children returning from work — for violating a newly imposed curfew of which many had not been informed. The killings occurred on the first day of the Sinai Campaign.
incidents.evidence: Israeli military court convicted several officers and soldiers. The trial established the "manifestly illegal order" doctrine in Israeli military law. Annual commemorations and official apologies have since acknowledged the massacre; the historical fact pattern is not in serious dispute.

sources.label: Israeli MFA historical yearbook references (use with commission context)

incidents.title: Khan Yunis Massacre (1956)
incidents.summary: During the Sinai Campaign, Israeli forces entered Khan Yunis. Contemporary UN and later historical accounts document mass killings of Palestinian men in and around the town, with death-toll estimates commonly cited in the hundreds. The event remains one of the deadliest single episodes of the 1956 Gaza occupation period.
incidents.evidence: UNRWA and contemporaneous diplomatic reporting recorded large-scale civilian deaths. Later historical synthesis (including works drawing on Israeli and Palestinian archives) treats Khan Yunis 1956 as a documented mass-killing event even where exact body counts remain contested within a high range.

sources.label: UNISPAL / UNRWA historical Gaza documentation index
Britannica — Suez Crisis context for 1956 Sinai Campaign

incidents.title: Al-Samu Raid (1966)
incidents.location: As-Samu, West Bank (then under Jordanian control)
incidents.summary: Israeli forces conducted a large daylight raid on the West Bank village of as-Samu after a landmine killed three Israeli soldiers. Dozens of houses and a clinic were demolished; contemporaneous tallies put Palestinian dead in the teens to twenties, including civilians, with many more wounded. The raid provoked regional crisis and UN Security Council condemnation.
incidents.evidence: UN Security Council debate and Resolution 228 (1966) condemned the large-scale military action. Contemporary UN Truce Supervision and Jordanian/Israeli reporting document house demolitions and civilian casualties. Historians treat as-Samu as a major pre-1967 escalation, not a disputed rumor.

sources.label: UNISPAL — Security Council debate on as-Samu

incidents.title: USS Liberty Attack — 34 U.S. Sailors Killed
incidents.summary: Israeli air and naval forces attacked the USS Liberty, a clearly marked U.S. Navy technical research ship, during the Six-Day War. 34 American servicemen were killed and 171 wounded. Israel apologized and paid reparations, calling the attack a case of mistaken identity. Surviving crew members and several later inquiries have disputed that account; official U.S. investigations accepted the accident framing while documenting command and identification failures.
incidents.evidence: U.S. Navy Court of Inquiry, NSA/State Department FRUS records, and Israeli inquiry materials form the documentary floor. Death and injury counts are not disputed. Attribution of intent remains contested — labeled verified for the attack itself and official findings, with honest note that motive is disputed.

sources.label: U.S. State Department FRUS — USS Liberty (Vol. XIX, Doc. 284 context)
U.S. Navy history — USS Liberty attack summary

incidents.summary: Israeli civilian settlements in occupied territory have expanded for decades, accompanied by land seizures, home demolitions, movement restrictions, and settler violence against Palestinians. incidents.evidence: ICJ advisory opinions (2004 wall; 2024 occupation), UNSC Resolution 2334, B'Tselem settlement data, and Peace Now tracking form the public floor. incidents.summary: Black September militants took Israeli Olympic athletes hostage; the crisis ended with eleven Israeli athletes and a German police officer dead after a failed rescue at Fürstenfeldbruck airfield. incidents.evidence: German investigations, Israeli government casualty lists, IOC records, and multi-decade historiography form a multi-source floor. legalCases.title: ICC Arrest Warrants — Netanyahu and Gallant
legalCases.ruling: Pre-Trial Chamber I issued arrest warrants for Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity including: starvation as a method of warfare, murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts.
legalCases.significance: First arrest warrants issued for a sitting Western-allied head of state since the ICC's establishment. ICC member states (124 countries) are legally obligated to arrest Netanyahu if he enters their territory.

legalCases.title: ICJ Advisory Opinion — Legality of the Occupation
legalCases.ruling: The court found Israel's continued presence in the Occupied Palestinian Territory is unlawful, that settlements violate Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention, and that Israel's policies amount to de facto annexation and apartheid.
legalCases.significance: First time the world's highest court applied the term "apartheid" to Israeli policies. Called on all states to distinguish between Israel and the occupied territories in their dealings.

legalCases.title: ICJ Advisory Opinion — Separation Wall
legalCases.ruling: The court ruled 14-1 that the construction of the wall in the occupied Palestinian territory is contrary to international law. Israel was obligated to dismantle it and make reparation for damage caused.
legalCases.significance: Israel refused to comply. 22 years later, the wall remains, now 712 km long, with 85% built inside the West Bank rather than on the Green Line.

legalCases.title: Kahan Commission — Sabra and Shatila
legalCases.ruling: Found that Defense Minister Ariel Sharon bore "personal responsibility" for failing to prevent the Phalangist massacre of civilians in the Sabra and Shatila camps; recommended his removal from the defense portfolio.
legalCases.significance: Rare official Israeli government finding of personal ministerial responsibility for mass civilian killing by allied forces under Israeli military control of the perimeter.

legalCases.title: UN Commission of Inquiry — Great March of Return (2018)
legalCases.court: UN Human Rights Council Commission of Inquiry
legalCases.ruling: Found reasonable grounds that Israeli snipers intentionally shot children, medics, journalists, and persons with disabilities during the 2018 Gaza protests, amounting to possible war crimes and crimes against humanity.
legalCases.significance: Highest-level UN investigative finding on the 2018 protest killings; Israel rejected the mandate and findings.

legalCases.title: B'Tselem / HRW / Amnesty — Apartheid Characterizations
legalCases.court: Leading human-rights organizations (not a court judgment)
legalCases.ruling: B'Tselem (2021), Human Rights Watch (2021), and Amnesty International (2022) each concluded that Israeli authorities commit the crime against humanity of apartheid (and, for HRW/Amnesty, persecution) against Palestinians.
legalCases.significance: NGO legal characterizations — not ICJ/ICC final judgments. Tracked here so readers can distinguish court orders from organizational findings.

legalCases.title: UN Security Council Resolution 2334 — Settlements
legalCases.ruling: Reaffirmed that Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem, have no legal validity and constitute a flagrant violation under international law; demanded that Israel immediately and completely cease all settlement activities.
legalCases.significance: U.S. abstained under Obama rather than vetoing — a rare break from automatic cover. The resolution remains the core Security Council floor on settlement illegality.

legalCases.title: UN Security Council Resolution 242 — Land for Peace Framework
legalCases.ruling: Called for withdrawal of Israeli armed forces from territories occupied in the 1967 conflict and for respect for the right of every state in the area to live in peace within secure and recognized boundaries.
legalCases.significance: Foundational post-1967 diplomatic framework still cited in every major peace process and occupation-law debate. Implementation remains incomplete and contested.

legalCases.title: UN Fact-Finding Mission on the Gaza Conflict (Goldstone)
legalCases.court: UN Human Rights Council Fact-Finding Mission
legalCases.ruling: Found evidence of war crimes and possible crimes against humanity by Israeli forces and Palestinian armed groups during Operation Cast Lead; recommended accountability processes in national and international forums.
legalCases.significance: The most cited UN fact-finding product on the 2008–09 Gaza war. Later public statements by the chair about reassessing some conclusions do not erase the mission's underlying multi-source field documentation still used by courts and scholars.

legalCases.title: UN Security Council Resolution 2712 — Gaza Humanitarian Pause Framework (2023)
legalCases.ruling: Called for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses and corridors throughout Gaza to enable full, rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access; demanded compliance by all parties with international humanitarian law.
legalCases.significance: Documents the Security Council floor on humanitarian access early in the Gaza war; implementation and pause duration remained contested.

legalCases.title: UN General Assembly ES-10/L.31 — Immediate Ceasefire Demand (Dec 2023)
legalCases.ruling: Demanded an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and ensuring humanitarian access; adopted by large majority with U.S. voting no.
legalCases.significance: Records the GA majority posture versus U.S. veto politics in the Security Council — structural diplomatic map of isolation vs cover.

legalCases.title: UN Security Council Resolution 2728 — Ramadan Ceasefire Demand (2024)
legalCases.ruling: Demanded an immediate ceasefire for the month of Ramadan leading to a lasting sustainable ceasefire, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and ensuring humanitarian access; adopted 14-0 with one abstention (United States).
legalCases.significance: Documents a rare post-Oct-7 Security Council ceasefire demand that passed with U.S. abstention rather than veto — a diplomatic floor often contrasted with later U.S. vetoes of stronger texts.

legalCases.title: ICJ Order — South Africa v. Israel Additional Measures (May 24, 2024 Rafah)
legalCases.ruling: In the ongoing Genocide Convention case, the Court ordered Israel to immediately halt its military offensive, and any other action in the Rafah Governorate, which may inflict on the Palestinian group in Gaza conditions of life that could bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part; reaffirmed prior provisional measures and aid access obligations.
legalCases.significance: Tightens ICJ provisional architecture around the Rafah offensive specifically — separate from the January/March 2024 orders. Implementation and interpretation remain contested; the order itself is the primary record.

legalCases.title: UN General Assembly ES-10/23 — Admission of Palestine (May 2024)
legalCases.ruling: Determined that the State of Palestine is qualified for membership in the United Nations and recommended that the Security Council reconsider the matter favorably; upgraded Palestine's rights and privileges as an observer State pending full membership.
legalCases.significance: Documents the GA majority posture on Palestinian statehood after a U.S. Security Council veto blocked full membership — structural diplomatic map of GA vs. UNSC veto politics parallel to ceasefire votes.

legalCases.title: ICJ Order — South Africa v. Israel Provisional Measures (Jan 26, 2024 Detailed Floor)
legalCases.ruling: Found it plausible that rights under the Genocide Convention are at risk; ordered Israel to take all measures within its power to prevent genocidal acts, prevent and punish incitement, ensure humanitarian assistance, and preserve evidence. Distinct depth entry for the January floor order (complementing the ongoing case card and later Rafah order).
legalCases.significance: First ICJ provisional-measures order against Israel under the Genocide Convention — foundational legal posture for all subsequent orders in Case 192.

legalCases.title: UNHRC Independent International Commission of Inquiry — OPT (Ongoing)
legalCases.court: UN Human Rights Council Commission of Inquiry
legalCases.ruling: Standing Commission of Inquiry continues to investigate all alleged violations of international humanitarian and human rights law in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and Israel, including post–October 7 conduct by all parties. Periodic reports document patterns of civilian harm, settlement violence, and accountability gaps.
legalCases.significance: Ongoing multi-year UN investigative architecture distinct from one-off fact-finding missions (Goldstone, GMR). Provides continuous public-record reporting stream used by courts, states, and civil society.

legalCases.title: Nicaragua v. Germany — Genocide Convention Intervention (ICJ 2024)
legalCases.ruling: Nicaragua instituted proceedings against Germany alleging failure to prevent genocide and complicity via arms exports to Israel; the Court issued provisional-measures orders addressing Germany's obligations under the Genocide Convention and arms-export diligence. Parallel diplomatic-legal pressure track on third-state enablement.
legalCases.significance: Extends Genocide Convention litigation beyond Israel itself to major arms-exporting third states — structural map of third-state responsibility claims adjacent to U.S. FMF enablement questions.

legalCases.title: UN Security Council Resolution 2735 — Gaza Ceasefire Phases (June 2024)
legalCases.ruling: Welcomed a ceasefire proposal encompassing three phases (temporary ceasefire and hostage/prisoner exchange; permanent cessation and reconstruction; multi-year pathway for a two-state solution) and called on all parties to implement it fully.
legalCases.significance: Records a U.S.-backed Security Council ceasefire architecture after months of veto politics — distinct from earlier 2712/2728 humanitarian-pause and Ramadan texts.

legalCases.title: U.S. UNSC Veto Cluster — Gaza Ceasefire Drafts (2023–2024)
legalCases.ruling: The United States vetoed multiple Security Council draft resolutions calling for immediate ceasefires or stronger humanitarian language, while allowing limited texts (e.g., 2712, 2728 with abstention, 2735) to pass. Pattern card for the veto architecture of diplomatic cover during the Gaza war.
legalCases.significance: Documents structural diplomatic enablement via veto power parallel to FMF/weapons pipelines — the UN voting map of isolation vs cover.
